idea: Caches trade a bounded set of slots for fewer misses. LRU protects recent keys; LFU protects frequent ones and breaks ties by recency.
steps: Replay requests in order; every miss inserts the key.
Update either the recency list or frequency buckets.
Record evictions and compare hit counts on the same trace.
example: With two slots, a a b c a gives LRU one hit but LFU two: LFU preserves the frequent a.
concepts: A map points directly to linked-list nodes, avoiding scans.
Each bucket orders keys with equal frequency by recency.
An exact LFU without aging can protect yesterday’s hot keys.
question: Is LFU always better?
answer: No. A scan, a hot set and a changing workload reward different policies. This exact educational LFU has no decay; Redis uses different production approximations.
challenge: Compare a hot key followed by a completely new working set.
cost: O(1) amortized access bookkeeping; rendering a full snapshot costs O(capacity).
